items.title: Potential fix for code scanning alert no. 226: Clear-text logging of sensitive information
items.body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/joshuaswarren/remnic/security/code-scanning/226](https://github.com/joshuaswarren/remnic/security/code-scanning/226)

General fix: avoid logging exception messages or any values derived from parsed config/env secrets; log only fixed, non-sensitive diagnostic text.

Best minimal fix (without changing functionality): in `packages/remnic-cli/src/commands/codegraph.ts`, replace both vulnerable error logs with constant/sanitized messages:
1. In the inner `catch` around config parse, remove interpolation of `err` (including `err.name`) and keep a static failure message.
2. In the outer `catch`, stop printing `err.message` and print a static generic command-failure message.

This preserves behavior (command still fails with exit code 1 and gives operator guidance) while removing clear-text secret exposure paths.

items.title: Potential fix for code scanning alert no. 227: Clear-text logging of sensitive information
items.body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/joshuaswarren/remnic/security/code-scanning/227](https://github.com/joshuaswarren/remnic/security/code-scanning/227)

Best fix: stop logging exception-derived free text (`err.message`, `String(err)`, and tainted interpolation context) in this command, and replace with fixed, non-sensitive messages plus optional non-sensitive error type classification.

In `packages/remnic-cli/src/commands/export-okf.ts`:
- In the inner `catch (err)` (config load/parse), replace the current interpolated message (line 51) with a constant message that does **not** include `configPath` or any `err` data.
- In the outer `catch (err)`, replace `console.error(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));` with a constant message (or constant + safe code), so no exception payload is emitted.
- Keep existing exit behavior unchanged (`process.exitCode = 1; return;`) so functionality remains the same except for safer logs.

No new imports or dependencies are needed.

items.title: fix(security): stop logging config-derived text on a failed load
items.body:
## Summary

Closes the last two open code-scanning alerts, `#226` and `#227`
(`js/clear-text-logging`), by removing config-derived output from the
failed-load path entirely.

## Why the previous fix did not close them

The post-merge CodeQL analysis of `2133fcada` dropped from 6 results to 3 — the
three `js/polynomial-redos` alerts closed — but both clear-text alerts stayed
open on `refs/heads/main`, reported against that exact commit. CodeQL treats the
config file's text as sensitive once a credential is parsed out of it, so no
output derived from that file can clear the rule.

Four attempts, one lesson: the only amount of config-derived logging that is
safe is none.

| attempt | why it failed |
|---|---|
| redact the parsed object | taint cannot see through a generic `redact<T>()`; a key deny-list is only as complete as its last edit |
| describe the object's shape | still reads every value, including `openaiApiKey` |
| scan the file text for key names | still tainted; and a malformed file repeatedly found ways to have a value read as a key (invalid scalars, mismatched closers, empty members) |
| **log nothing derived from it** | this PR |

## What stays

The inner `try`/`catch` — that is the fix for the actual defect. `parseConfig`
error text embeds raw config values (an unresolved `${...}` placeholder is the
key's own text), and it no longer reaches stderr. The commands print the error
class and the config path, and say plainly that values are never printed.

## What goes

`config-key-report.ts` and its 190-line suite: 223 lines of scanner whose only
consumer was a log line that should not exist. Deleted rather than left beside
an unused path.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit -p packages/remnic-cli` clean for both changed files.
- `scripts/check-regex-safety.mjs` exits 0 (the deleted scanner's patterns are
  gone with it).
- No `rawText`, `reportConfigKeys`, or `config-key-report` reference remains in
  `packages/remnic-cli/src`.
- Expected result on merge: alerts `#226` and `#227` close, leaving zero open
  code-scanning alerts and zero open Dependabot alerts.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved configuration-load error messages to avoid exposing configuration-derived values, keys, or parser details.
  * Configuration failures now report only the configuration path, error type, and a clear fixed message.
  * Existing configuration files continue to be parsed, while missing files are handled safely with default settings.

* **Security**
  * Reduced the risk of sensitive configuration information appearing in command-line error output.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: fix(security): clear all five CodeQL alerts
items.body:
## Summary

Clears all five open CodeQL alerts.

### js/clear-text-logging (HIGH) — #223, #220

`parseConfig` error strings embed raw config values: `resolveEnvVars` throws
`Malformed environment variable placeholder: <the value>` for `openaiApiKey`
and `localLlmApiKey`, and several rejects stringify the raw field. The
catch-all `console.error(err.message)` in the `codegraph` and `export-okf`
commands could therefore print key material.

Config loading now runs in its own try block, and on failure the commands print
the error class plus a config dump passed through a new `redactConfigForLog`.
Redaction is **by key name**, applied recursively, so a newly added
`anthropicApiKey` is masked by construction rather than by someone remembering
to add a pattern — a test pins exactly that case with a key the redactor was
never told about. The pattern mirrors `SENSITIVE_KEY_RE` in core's
admin-surfaces, the existing in-repo convention.

### js/polynomial-redos (HIGH) — #222, #219, #195

| site | defect | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `reconcile/cursor.ts` | `/\/+$/` backtracks quadratically on long slash runs that do not end in a slash | `stripTrailingSlashes`, a bounded character loop |
| `transfer/export-okf.ts` | `/^#\s+(.+)$/` — `\s+` and `.+` overlap, so a failed match backtracks over every split point | `/^#\s+(\S.*)$/`, disjoint capture boundary |
| `location/matching.ts` | `/^-+\|-+$/` quadratic on dash runs in isolation | single-character strips, which the preceding `/[^a-z0-9]+/` collapse makes complete |

## Verification

Discrimination measured per site with file-level restores (not `git stash` —
it is repo-global across worktrees):

- `cursor.ts` reverted → its timing test fails.
- `export-okf.ts` reverted with the `firstHeading` export kept → its timing
  test fails.
- `matching.ts`: a timing test could **not** discriminate, because the collapse
  already bounds the trim's input, so it was replaced with a test of the
  invariant the strips depend on (no edge may hold two dashes). Weakening the
  collapse to `/[^a-z0-9]/` fails it.

Suites: `matching` 4/4, `cursor` 12/12, `export-okf` 11/11, `redact-config`
3/3. `tsc --noEmit -p packages/remnic-core` clean; the CLI's remaining
resolution errors are the unbuilt-workspace artifact a fresh worktree always
shows (127 of them on clean `main` too), not from this change.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Configuration diagnostics show detected keys and unresolved placeholders without exposing sensitive values.
  * Reports indicate when scanning stops early or reaches the key limit.
  * Empty, malformed, and whitespace-only configuration files are handled more reliably.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved configuration loading and error reporting for code graph and OKF export commands.

* **Performance**
  * Improved processing of unusually long inputs, including location tags, peer identifiers, headings, and configuration text.

* **Tests**
  * Expanded coverage for redaction, parsing edge cases, Unicode, duplicate keys, and large inputs.

items.title: chore(deps): close every open Dependabot alert
items.body:
## Summary

Closes every open Dependabot alert.

| package | before | after | alerts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hono` | 4.12.29 | 4.13.3 | 4 (one low, three medium) |
| `@hono/node-server` | 1.19.14 | 1.19.15 | 1 medium |
| `postcss` | 8.5.17 | 8.5.26 | 2 (one **high**) |
| `tar` | 7.5.20 | 7.5.22 | 1 medium |
| `torch` (pip) | 2.12.1 | 2.13.0+cu126 | 1 low |

All four npm packages are transitive. `@hono/node-server` needed a
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` override because the `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` range is
`^1.19.9 || ^2.0.5`, so a plain resolver update jumps to the 2.x major; the
override pins the patched 1.x instead. The existing `overrides:` block was
extended rather than a second mechanism introduced.

`torch` follows the file's existing `==<version>+cu126` pin style.

## Verification

- `node scripts/pnpm.mjs install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds.
- Lockfile resolves `hono@4.13.3`, `@hono/node-server@1.19.15`,
  `postcss@8.5.26`, `tar@7.5.22` — each at or above its first patched version.
- Lockfile regenerated by the pinned wrapper (`pnpm@10.32.1`), not hand-edited.
- No unrelated dependency moved; `nanoid` 3.3.15 -> 3.3.18 rides along as
  postcss's own dependency.

items.title: chore(ci): gate link vocabularies, batch thread requests, document three defect classes
items.body:
## Summary

Five process fixes for failures this run actually hit. A sixth candidate was **measured and rejected** rather than shipped as noise.

### Shipped

1. **`scripts/check-nav-link-vocabularies.mjs`** (wired into the `checks` job) fails when the shared navigation parser does not know a link type the stepper accepts or that is actually persisted. Three lists had drifted apart silently: the parser rejected `follows`/`references`/`related` — which real frontmatter carries, so a traversal over stored links dropped those neighbors — and `supersedes`, which the stepper accepts. It took **two review rounds** to find. The unit test replays that exact pre-fix divergence and asserts each missing type is attributed to the list that requires it.
2. **`scripts/pr-review-threads.mjs`** issues ONE aliased query for every PR and ONE aliased mutation for every thread, instead of 2N requests. The naive per-PR loop exhausted the GraphQL point budget **three times in this run**, each time leaving `unresolved-review-threads` red until the budget refilled — roughly two and a half hours of pure waiting. Smoke-tested live against a real PR.
3. **`AGENTS.md` pattern 46** — enumerate keys with `getOwnPropertyNames`, read them with `hasOwn`, and treat present-with-`undefined` as invalid rather than absent. Two allow-list bypasses shipped one review round apart on exactly this mismatch (inherited property, then non-enumerable property).
4. **`AGENTS.md` pattern 47** — never annotate a frozen `as const` array `readonly T[]`; it widens the derived literal union back to `string`. This shipped as a regression *inside a hardening fix*. Includes the `@ts-expect-error` pin that makes a future widening fail the build, since an unused directive is itself an error.
5. **`AGENTS.md` pattern 48** — every claim in a PR body, module header, or changeset must name the code or test enforcing it, or be weakened to what is true. Two false claims were caught by reviewers this run ("structurally incapable of carrying content" on a validator that accepted prose; "internal helper" on an exported module).

### Measured and rejected

Per the README ground rule — run a condition against the tree before shipping it:

- A regex for the pattern-47 widening (`: readonly T[] = Object.freeze([...])`) matches **13 legitimate frozen data arrays** (seed vocabularies, prose frames, fixture memories) where no `(typeof X)[number]` union is derived and the annotation is the intended type. Separating them needs two facts in different places, so it is not a single-line signature. Receipt recorded in `.omp/rules/README.md`; the remedy lives in pattern 47.

## Test plan

- `node scripts/check-nav-link-vocabularies.mjs` — passes on current `main` (parser knows 9 types, covering 5 stepper and 5 persisted), locking in the batch-9 fix.
- `node --test tests/check-nav-link-vocabularies.test.mjs tests/pr-review-threads.test.mjs` — 11/11.
- `node scripts/pr-review-threads.mjs list joshuaswarren/remnic 2756` — exercised against the live API in a single request.

items.title: feat(recall): check the state-view zero-diff compatibility promise
items.body:
## Summary

Makes #1952's compatibility promise checkable: "current items unchanged (**zero diff for existing users when no historical item qualifies**)".

That promise had no enforcement. The render path could gain a prefix, add a trailing space, or reorder a current-only result set and nothing would notice — the state-view feature would silently change injected context for users who never had a historical item to show.

`checkStateViewZeroDiff` compares the baseline injection against the annotated one and fails on any difference: `current_line_changed` names the offending memory id, and `order_changed` covers the case where every line matches but the sequence moved, since injected order drives what the agent reads first. Comparison is exact, so a renderer's trailing space is a diff.

The two ok reasons are deliberately distinguishable, documented in the module header: `unchanged` means the guarantee was checked and held, `no_historical_items` means it does not apply to this comparison. A caller can tell "verified" from "not applicable" instead of reading a bare true.

Labels come from the existing state-view type rather than a second list, and a non-`current` label in the baseline throws, since the baseline is by definition the pre-feature output.

Part of #1952 (guard helper; wiring it into a pipeline test is a later slice, so the issue stays open).

## Test plan

- `NODE_OPTIONS=--conditions=remnic-source npx tsx --test packages/remnic-core/src/recall-state-view-zero-diff.test.ts` — 11/11
- Covers identical lists, a changed line, a reorder, a trailing-space diff, the not-applicable path, a labelled baseline, unknown labels, duplicate ids, and input immutability.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added validation for unchanged recall state-view text and memory ordering when only current items are present.
  - Reports whether validation is verified, not applicable, or identifies changed text or ordering.

- **Tests**

items.title: feat(shared-context): resolve shared authority to the least privilege by default
items.body:
## Summary

Implements #1957's authority resolution: `informational | advisory | binding`, "default `informational`; `binding` requires explicit flag", and "legacy items without the envelope → `informational` + no expiry (least privilege, pattern 36)".

The security property is that nothing reaches `binding` by accident. Absent, non-string, and unrecognized authority values all resolve to `informational` — no case-folding, no trimming, so `"BINDING"` and `" binding"` are unrecognized data rather than near-misses that get normalized into privilege. A stored `"binding"` without the explicit opt-in **downgrades to advisory** rather than throwing, because a legacy item carrying that value is data, not a caller bug; the reasoning is in a comment at the branch.

`allowBinding` is the security switch, so a non-boolean throws instead of being coerced — a truthy `"false"` string must never enable binding.

The classes and type come from `governance.ts` (`SHARED_AUTHORITIES`) and are re-exported, not redefined, so there is one list. `compareSharedAuthority` is total: equal classes return 0 and an unknown class sorts as `informational` rather than throwing, so a mixed list stays sortable.

Part of #1957 (resolution helpers; read/write path wiring is a later slice, so the issue stays open).

## Test plan

- `NODE_OPTIONS=--conditions=remnic-source npx tsx --test packages/remnic-core/src/shared-context/authority-precedence.test.ts` — 10/10
- **Mutation-checked**: removing the `allowBinding` requirement so `binding` is honored unconditionally fails the flag test, so the security gate is genuinely asserted rather than incidentally true.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added shared-authority resolution with clear precedence ordering.
  * Added least-privilege defaults for missing or invalid authority values.
  * Added safeguards requiring explicit approval for binding-level authority.
  * Added authority comparison and deterministic ordering support.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of unknown, invalid, and non-boolean authority inputs.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: feat(activity): stamp journal memories with their source and day
items.body:
## Summary

Implements #1987's provenance requirement: journal-derived memories "additionally carry `structuredAttributes.journalSource: "vault"` so review UI and future audits can distinguish vault-sourced journal candidates from memoryDir ones. **String values only**", plus the `journal` / `journal-day:<date>` tags and the `valid_at` pin the issue specifies.

`buildJournalMemoryProvenance` enforces the string-only rule in the return type, and a test asserts every attribute value is a string so a future field cannot smuggle a number or object into a shape the review UI reads.

The source is validated through the existing journal-source parser rather than a second allow-list, and an unknown value throws instead of defaulting to `memoryDir` — defaulting would defeat the one thing the attribute exists to do. The date must be a real calendar day (`2026-02-30` is refused, not rolled over), and the helper never reads the clock: the day comes from the caller so a re-run pins the same `valid_at`.

Part of #1987 (provenance builder; the review-gated extraction pass that consumes it is a later slice, so the issue stays open).

## Test plan

- `NODE_OPTIONS=--conditions=remnic-source npx tsx --test packages/remnic-core/src/activity/journal-vault-provenance.test.ts` — 10/10
- Covers both sources differing only in the attribute value, the exact two-tag array and its order, string-only attribute values, unknown source rejection, malformed and impossible dates, and deep-equality across calls.

items.title: feat(activity): compute an order-stable weekly snapshot config hash
items.body:
## Summary

Computes the `configHash` that #2052's snapshot key already requires. `weekly-persist.ts` has consumed a `configHash` since it landed, but nothing produced one — so every caller would have invented its own, and two callers would have disagreed, silently splitting or colliding stored snapshots.

`computeWeeklyConfigHash` is stable across category array order and object key insertion order, because a harmless reorder must not orphan every stored snapshot. It changes for every semantic change the issue names: renamed category, added category, removed category, different timezone, different week start — each tested individually.

Duplicate category ids throw rather than hashing, since two definitions for one id make the snapshot key ambiguous. The digest length is asserted in a test so a future algorithm swap is a visible, deliberate change rather than a silent one that invalidates stored snapshots.

Part of #2052 (hash helper; the persist call site passes its own value today, so wiring is a later slice and the issue stays open).

## Test plan

- `NODE_OPTIONS=--conditions=remnic-source npx tsx --test packages/remnic-core/src/activity/timeline/week-config-hash.test.ts` — 12/12
- Covers order-independence on both axes, all five semantic changes, duplicate ids, blank field rejection, digest shape, and that the caller's array is not sorted in place.

* **Bug Fixes**
